text:
Ben H: Hey all, first week question — I'm trying to access resources in the team-b namespace but `kubectl get pods -n team-b` returns Forbidden. I can still `kubectl get namespaces`. My kubeconfig is a giant merged file from multiple clusters. What's the recommended way to get a clean kubeconfig for a single cluster/user? Also is using `--as` impersonation something devs can do for debugging?

Lina M: Welcome Ben! :wave: If your kubeconfig is merged, try this while the correct context is selected:
```
kubectl config view --flatten --minify > /tmp/kube-ben
export KUBECONFIG=/tmp/kube-ben
kubectl config current-context
```
That gives you a minimal file for the active context which stops tooling from accidentally using another user entry.

Carlos: Also run `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n team-b` to see what your current creds actually allow. If your org uses OIDC/SSO, you might need to refresh your provider token (aws/gcloud/okta) — merged kubeconfigs often point at the wrong user block.

Ben H: Ran `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n team-b` and it says "no". Strange that I can list namespaces though.

Lina M: Listing namespaces can be granted separately. Most likely you just need a RoleBinding in team-b for your user or group. You can ask infra to apply something like (they prefer to apply, not you):
```
kubectl create rolebinding ben-view-teamb --clusterrole=view --user=ben@redwood.com -n team-b
```
That gives view permissions scoped to the namespace.

Carlos: Quick note on impersonation: `--as` is admin-sensitive. Granting someone the ability to impersonate identities requires extra RBAC (system:auth-delegator etc.) and infra will not do that lightly. If you need debug access, ask for a timeboxed RoleBinding instead.

infra-bot: Policy reminder: do not request cluster-admin or permanent broad bindings. For temporary elevation, open an infra ticket with desired verbs/resources and duration. All changes are logged.

Ben H: Makes sense. One more Q: for local dev and tooling (tilt/skaffold) is there a recommended pattern when we want a kubeconfig that only contains a single context/serviceaccount? Do teams create serviceaccounts for devs?

Lina M: Best practice is a namespaced serviceaccount with minimal permissions used by CI, and for local dev we request infra to mint a short-lived kubeconfig tied to a timeboxed RoleBinding. For CI you can use SA tokens projected into pods. For local dev ask infra to create the SA + RoleBinding and they can hand you a flattened kubeconfig.

Ben H: Filing ticket now (INF-1223) with the verbs I need and timeframe. Using the flattened kubeconfig trick I can `describe pods` in team-b after infra applied the RoleBinding. Thanks everyone for the pointer! :tada:
